outline: Constitutive KIT signaling and multisystem mast-cell mediator effects
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Systemic mastocytosis is a clonal mast-cell neoplasm commonly driven by an activating KIT mutation, most often KIT D816V. Constitutive KIT receptor-tyrosine-kinase signaling permits stem-cell-factor-independent mast-cell survival and proliferation; mediator release and tissue infiltration produce multisystem symptoms.
vignette: A 42-year-old woman has recurrent episodes of flushing, pruritus, abdominal cramping, diarrhea, and light-headedness. Several tan-brown skin lesions become raised and erythematous when rubbed. Her baseline serum tryptase concentration is persistently elevated. Bone marrow biopsy shows multifocal dense aggregates of spindle-shaped mast cells expressing CD117 and CD25.
lead: Which of the following molecular abnormalities most likely underlies this patient's disorder?
correct: Constitutive activation of the KIT receptor tyrosine kinase, most commonly due to a D816V mutation
distractors: Constitutive JAK2 activation due to a V617F mutation
A FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion producing constitutive platelet-derived growth factor receptor signaling
A BCR-ABL1 fusion producing constitutive ABL tyrosine kinase signaling
Loss of NF1 function causing unrestrained RAS signaling in neural-crest-derived cells
distractor_notes: JAK2 V617F is strongly associated with classic myeloproliferative neoplasms such as polycythemia vera, essential thrombocythemia, and primary myelofibrosis; it does not best explain a clonal mast-cell disorder with elevated tryptase and mast-cell aggregates.
FIP1L1-PDGFRA is characteristic of certain myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia. Systemic mastocytosis is instead most commonly driven by activating KIT, especially D816V.
BCR-ABL1 drives chronic myeloid leukemia and some acute lymphoblastic leukemias. The mast-cell phenotype, tryptase elevation, and CD117-positive aggregates point to KIT-driven mastocytosis.
NF1 loss increases RAS signaling and predisposes to neurofibromas and other tumors, but it does not explain this classic systemic mastocytosis phenotype.
key_expl: This patient has systemic mastocytosis, suggested by recurrent mast-cell mediator symptoms, Darier-type urtication of pigmented lesions, persistently elevated basal tryptase, and clonal mast-cell aggregates in bone marrow. KIT encodes CD117, a receptor tyrosine kinase that regulates mast-cell growth and survival. Activating KIT mutations produce ligand-independent signaling; KIT D816V is the most common driver in systemic mastocytosis.
objective: Explain systemic mastocytosis as a clonal mast-cell disorder driven most commonly by constitutive KIT D816V receptor-tyrosine-kinase signaling.
clues: pigmented lesions that urticate with rubbing
